root_cause: PromptBase.check_choice did an exact `value.strip() in self.choices` membership test, so there was no way to accept 'paul' for choice 'Paul'. New feature: an opt-in case_sensitive flag.
best_solution: Add `case_sensitive: bool = True` to PromptBase.__init__ (store as self.case_sensitive), to all three `ask` overloads plus the implementation, and pass it through to `cls(...)`. In check_choice: when case_sensitive is True keep the exact membership test, otherwise compare `value.strip().lower()` against `[c.lower() for c in self.choices]`. In process_response, after the choice passes validation and case_sensitive is False, return the canonical choice rather than what the user typed: `self.response_type(self.choices[[c.lower() for c in self.choices].index(value.lower())])`. So 'FoO' comes back as 'foo'. Prompt rendering is unchanged ('[foo/bar] (baz)'), and an invalid input still prints 'Please select one of the available options'.
acceptable_alternatives: Adding the kwarg anywhere in the signatures works, since the tests pass it by keyword. Any normalisation works (casefold, or a dict mapping lower to original) as long as check_choice accepts case variants and process_response returns the original spelling from `choices`, not the raw input.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_prompt.py::test_prompt_str_case_insensitive: Prompt.ask('what is your name', console=..., choices=['foo','bar'], default='baz', case_sensitive=False, stream=StringIO('egg\nFoO')) must return exactly 'foo' (the canonical choice, not 'FoO'). The console output must be exactly 'what is your name [foo/bar] (baz): Please select one of the available options\nwhat is your name [foo/bar] (baz): '. The existing prompt tests must keep passing, which means the default stays case-sensitive.
locating_signals: The statement names `Prompt.ask`, the kwarg `case_sensitive=False` and its default True. `rich.prompt` is in the import. The function to change (check_choice / process_response in rich/prompt.py) is not named, but it is the only choice-validation code and a grep for 'choices' finds it at once.
our_outcome_summary: All four configs (v4, v6, v7, v8) failed with EMPTY patches (patch_chars=0) after 313-366 s. v4, v6 and v8 ended on litellm ContextWindowExceededError (32k context), and v7 hit the 6-minute session timeout. The agent found the right file and started at the right spot: it tried to add case_sensitive to the PromptBase docstring. Every edit_file call came out malformed. Its new_string ran into a closing docstring `"""`, and the Gemma tool-call serializer then broke apart. The text `,old_string:` ended up inside the new_string value, and pieces of the docstring such as 'choices (List[str], optional)' became extra argument keys. So old_string was never present, and the harness replied 'mandatory input parameters are not present: old_string'. The model repeated the same malformed call 141/131/142/125 times (v4/v6/v7/v8) until the context or time budget ran out, and no edit ever landed. Separately, an earlier sw1_v1 run did land a patch. It threaded the kwarg through and made check_choice case-insensitive, but it still failed test_prompt_str_case_insensitive with `assert 'FoO' == 'foo'`. It never changed process_response to return the canonical choice.
generalizable_lesson: Two lessons. (1) Harness: detect the same tool error repeated with identical arguments. After 2 or 3 repeats, force a change of strategy: a smaller edit anchored on a single code line away from docstrings or triple quotes, a line-range or whole-file write, or a sed/python rewrite through run_command. Also sanitize or escape `"""` in edit arguments. A parse failure that keeps repeating should never burn the whole budget. (2) Semantics: when adding a case-insensitive or normalised matching option, return the canonical stored value (the original spelling from the choices list), not the user's raw input. Tests usually assert the normalised return value, not just that validation passes. Also thread a new kwarg through every overload, the classmethod factory and the constructor call.
